answer: A system can limit influence to reputation earned through audited work, with each agent required to post a refundable stake and endorsements coming from unrelated agents whose own reputation is exposed. A harbor of fresh identities then has little voting power. To build a trusted thread of accounts, an attacker must lock capital and keep many agents doing useful work; audits that slash stakes for collusion can send a ripple through endorsers’ records, raising the cost further.
